items.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022
items.q: sometimes they sounded angry, over the top with Pharoah Sanders and so forth

ctx.x: Well my interest was actually how he created this intense feeling of playing. I mean he was an artist. I mean he was almost like, you know he would be able to really just delve on just one of two things you know, not intricate but I mean to get that feeling of, I mean I have some cuts you know that he goes really — it’s not — analytically it’s not really a big thing but I mean the creation that he really has applied. I mean he was — that was the thing actually I suppose, and everybody does feel that way too when…

What about his later — well not specifically “Ascension” but some of the LPs near the end of his life were — I’m trying to think of the word — sometimes they sounded angry, over the top with Pharoah Sanders and so forth, did this still hold your interest?

No. No now even the club actually there were — there is one name that I don’t have over here, the flute player would come in actually and he would play and that would be — and he wouldn’t be able to do anything that Trane did actually. It was a little embarrassing.
